headline: Google released Nano Banana 2.1, a faster and cheaper image generation model that replaces its February version.
score_reason: Useful product release with a clear price cut, but an incremental update below Google's top image model.
importance_line: Developers and Google users get cheaper image generation, but the quality claims are Google's own and The Decoder notes its Pro model still often looks better.
summary: The Decoder reports that Google released Nano Banana 2.1, an image creation and editing model, and cut prices roughly in half, so a standard 1K image now costs 3.36 cents instead of 6.70. Google says it improves text in images and the consistency of characters across a conversation, and it is rolling out in the Gemini app, Google Search's AI Mode and Google's developer tools, while the older model shuts down on 29 Oct 2026.
